operations.specification: User registration endpoint for the Todo List service. Associates with the 'todo_list_users' table. The flow creates a new user record (requires a unique email and password), and sets 'is_verified' to false. On success, issues a verification email, blocks login until verification, and creates a pending user. This operation is public, does not require prior authentication, and is the entry point for new user onboarding. Email is globally unique and never modifiable. Password is stored as a secure hash and never returned.
operations.description:
This endpoint enables registration for new users by accepting a unique email address and password. The registration process involves strict email uniqueness enforcement—if a duplicate is detected in the 'todo_list_users' table, the system will reject the registration with a conflict error (referencing the 'email' unique index). The user's account is created in a pending (unverified) state, and a verification email is sent to the provided address using a unique token.

Only after verifying the email (using a separate operation) will the account become active (see 'is_verified' and 'is_active' fields in 'todo_list_users'). The password is securely stored as a salted cryptographic hash in 'password_hash' and never returned.

Upon successful registration, further authentication is blocked until email verification is completed. Users cannot change the email after registration, as enforced by the immutable 'email' column.

This registration operation is related to the email verification process, which users must complete before being able to log in.

Unsuccessful attempts due to invalid input or existing email result in clear error messages, following the validation rules established in the schema. Only user-facing data is returned—never internal account or security metadata.
operations.summary: Registers a new user in the todo_list_users table (pending verification).

requestBody.description: Registration payload, including email and password.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user info for verified or pending user (IAuthorized DTO).

operations.name: join

operations.specification: User login endpoint for the Todo List service. Operates on the 'todo_list_users' table for credential checks. Accepts email and password, verifies the account is active and 'is_verified' is true, then authenticates. On success, returns new JWT access and refresh tokens. Fails if credentials are invalid or account is not verified. Login is blocked until registration and email verification operations are fully completed. No user profile is returned except minimal token and identifying data.
operations.description:
Handles user login, validating submitted credentials against the 'todo_list_users' table using the combination of 'email' and securely-hashed 'password_hash' values. Only users marked as both 'is_verified' and 'is_active' can successfully receive tokens. The endpoint denies authentication if credentials are incorrect, if the email has not been verified, or the account is deactivated.

The operation returns JWT access and refresh tokens for valid users, leveraging the account's unique ID, and does not expose any internal security data or hashed passwords. Login requires that the email correspond to an existing, verified account in the user table.

The endpoint distinguishes only between correct and incorrect credentials, using generic error messages to prevent user enumeration or disclosing security-sensitive information.

Related operations include registration (for creating a pending account) and email verification (to activate the user).

Multiple concurrent sessions are supported via the 'todo_list_user_sessions' table, with each session generating its own tracked row for audit and security analysis.
operations.summary: Authenticates verified user from todo_list_users and issues tokens.

requestBody.description: Login credentials including email and password.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user info for authenticated user (IAuthorized DTO).

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Token refresh operation for the Todo List service. Operates on existing valid refresh tokens tied to user sessions (see 'todo_list_user_sessions' table). Accepts a currently valid refresh token, validates it against the session log, and, if correct and not expired or revoked, issues new access/refresh tokens. If the refresh token is invalid, missing, or expired, authentication is denied. Token life cycle and session management are tied to the user account and session log for security traceability.
operations.description:
Allows users to obtain a new access token by submitting a valid, unexpired refresh token. The operation cross-checks the provided token against the active session records in 'todo_list_user_sessions', confirming that the token is active, not expired ('expired_at' is null or in the future), and properly assigned to the user session indicated.

Session audits are enforced at the database level, tying each refresh token to its session and preventing reuse after logout or expiration. Expired, invalid, or missing tokens result in authentication failure. All critical information—such as token lifetime, IP, session metadata—is managed in the session log.

Refresh operations are central to secure, long-lived user authentication in stateless environments. No user profile or business data is returned except new token(s).

This endpoint is expected to be called by clients automatically on access token expiry. Failures trigger re-authentication via the login operation.
operations.summary: Issues new tokens for users with valid refresh tokens via todo_list_user_sessions.

requestBody.description: The valid refresh token to be exchanged for new tokens.

responseBody.description: Updated authentication tokens and user info for re-authenticated user (IAuthorized DTO).

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Handles user email verification flow. Uses 'todo_list_user_email_verifications' table. Accepts the unique verification token sent to user's email, checks if it has not expired or been previously consumed, and if valid, marks the user as 'is_verified' and enables login. Prevents login until verification is complete. If the token is invalid, expired, or already used, blocks activation and provides a suitable error message. This endpoint finalizes the user onboarding and switches the user's account from pending to active.
operations.description:
This endpoint accepts the email verification token (found in the 'todo_list_user_email_verifications' table) and, if valid, activates the associated user's account (sets 'is_verified' to true). Upon redemption, the 'consumed_at' timestamp is set, and the user's status transitions from pending to active, enabling the login operation.

If the verification token does not exist, has already been used ('consumed_at' not null), or is expired, the action is denied and the user remains unable to log in. Each verification token is single-use and time-limited, referencing the 'expires_at' and 'consumed_at' columns for validity.

This operation completes new user onboarding after registration. Invalid or expired tokens result in clear error messages, promoting security and usability.

Related operations are registration (creates the token), and login (requires successful verification before tokens are issued).

Failure scenarios cover incorrect usage and timeouts, maintaining auditability via the verification events log.
operations.summary: Finalizes user registration by activating account via email token in todo_list_user_email_verifications.

requestBody.description: Payload containing the email verification token.

responseBody.description: Minimal response indicating email verification success or failure.

operations.name: verifyEmail

operations.specification: User password reset request operation, tracking and handling via 'todo_list_user_password_resets'. Accepts email, issues a secure time-limited reset token if the account exists (does not reveal account presence), and delivers it to the user via email. Used when a user forgets their password. Never returns user account data; always responds generically regardless of presence. Rate limits enforced via resets log.
operations.description:
Initiates a password reset for user accounts. The endpoint accepts an email address and, if the corresponding user is present in 'todo_list_users', generates a unique single-use reset token (persisted in 'todo_list_user_password_resets'). This token is sent to the email on record. No information is leaked about whether the email exists, always replying success to prevent user enumeration.

All requests are audited; excessive attempts can be rate-limited using the password resets schema. The reset token includes strict expiration ('expires_at') and is unique per reset event ('reset_token').

The reset process itself is completed in a separate endpoint, where the user redeems the token by setting a new password.

Failed or expired token submissions handled in a companion operation.

Related entities: user (identity), resets (event log, token issue).

This operation never reveals presence of non-existent accounts for privacy and security reasons.
operations.summary: Initiates password reset process for user by generating time-limited reset token (todo_list_user_password_resets).

requestBody.description: Payload with user's email address for password reset request.

responseBody.description: Minimal response indicating reset initiation (never reveals account presence).

operations.name: requestPasswordReset

operations.specification: Completes user password reset flow using 'todo_list_user_password_resets'. Accepts reset token and new password, validates and consumes the token if valid, and updates the user's password in 'todo_list_users' (hashing it securely). Token is single-use and must not be expired or previously redeemed. On success, provides minimal confirmation. On failure, gives generic error to prevent abuse or enumeration.
operations.description:
Redemption endpoint for password reset: accepts the one-time reset token (from 'todo_list_user_password_resets') along with a new password. If the token is present, unconsumed, and not expired, the associated user's password is updated to the securely-hashed new value in 'todo_list_users', and the reset token event is marked as consumed ('consumed_at').

Used tokens cannot be re-used, and expired ones are rejected. Password reset is a sensitive operation and is audited in the event log for traceability, allowing enforcement of security/compliance policies.

Failing this operation (invalid or expired token) triggers a generic error message, preventing attackers from probing for valid tokens or emails.

Related flow requires a prior password reset initiation request, logged in the password resets table, and enforces the single-use, time-limited guarantee via database schema constraints.
operations.summary: Updates user's password via valid reset token in todo_list_user_password_resets; single-use only.

requestBody.description: Payload containing reset token and new password.

responseBody.description: Minimal response indicating password reset result.

operations.name: resetPassword

operations.specification: Authenticated endpoint for changing a user's password. Requires current (old) password and new password. Operates on 'todo_list_users' - verifies old password matches 'password_hash', then applies the update after securely hashing the new password. Fails if old password is incorrect. Only allowed for currently authenticated and active users.
operations.description:
Allows a logged-in user to change their account password by submitting both the current password and a valid new password. The operation compares the submitted current password against the cryptographic hash in 'password_hash' (from 'todo_list_users'), and if correct, stores the new hash securely.

If the current password is incorrect, the change is denied, and a relevant error is returned. The endpoint only operates for active, verified users, as enforced by the 'is_verified' and 'is_active' fields.

Password changes are logged with account 'updated_at' timestamp. All successful changes require validation of the proposed new password by policy.

Operation is related to authentication, password reset, and user entity management workflows. Failures are handled by consistent, informative error messages to assist the user.
operations.summary: Changes password for authenticated user in todo_list_users after current password verification.

requestBody.description: Payload with both current and new passwords for password change.

responseBody.description: Minimal response indicating success or reason for password change failure.

operations.name: changePassword

operations.specification: Logout endpoint to invalidate all active sessions and tokens for user. Connected to 'todo_list_user_sessions' for audit and token management. Requires authentication. When called, expires all session entries for the authenticated user, making all outstanding tokens invalid for further access.
operations.description:
Terminates all active user sessions, including access and refresh tokens, by updating or marking all corresponding entries as expired in the 'todo_list_user_sessions' table. This operation is exclusively for the authenticated user, requiring a valid session. Ensures any subsequent attempt to use old tokens results in authentication failure.

The endpoint updates session log entries (sets 'expired_at'), supporting full session invalidation as a security measure, useful for lost devices or account compromise recovery. Sessions are immediately invalidated and cannot be restored.

Operation is related to login, authentication, refresh, and session management endpoints. Success means user must re-authenticate to restore access.

Audit logs for each session are maintained for security analysis and troubleshooting. Error handling is robust, capturing rare failures in session update logic.
operations.summary: Logs out authenticated user, invalidating all todo_list_user_sessions, forcing re-authentication.

responseBody.description: Minimal response indicating successful logout.

operations.name: logout

operations.specification: Permanently deletes the currently authenticated user's account from 'todo_list_users' and all associated tables. Removes the account and all related data irreversibly, including todos, sessions, email verifications, and password reset logs. Operation is protected; requires strong authentication. All data is unrecoverable after success.
operations.description:
Irreversible removal endpoint that deletes the authenticated user’s account data from 'todo_list_users' and all dependent relations (todos, sessions, verifications, password resets). Sets 'deleted_at' on the user entity, disables login, and wipes associated data by policy.

This is a logged and traceable destructive operation: once successful, the account cannot be restored or re-registered. The operation ensures no credentials or residual personal data persist. Breaks all session tokens and revokes authentication immediately on execution, preventing any future login attempts for this email.

Unauthorized or unauthenticated requests are denied, ensuring only valid, verified users can erase their account. All error cases provide clear reasons for operation failure.
operations.summary: Permanently deletes authenticated user's account and related data; removes from todo_list_users and subsidiaries.

responseBody.description: Minimal response indicating successful or unsuccessful account deletion.

operations.name: eraseAccount

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the authenticated user's own profile by leveraging the users table (todo_list_users) as the source of truth. It supports typical "my profile" functionality in todo-based applications. The email address, display name, and account status/flags (is_verified, is_active) are included as read-only fields. Security and privacy are preserved by authenticating the request via the user's session and returning only the current user's data, never any other user's data. The system uses the JWT (or session) for identity; the path `/users/me` is a conventional alias for 'self'. This operation is critical for allowing users to view their current profile and account status, as required by many user-driven scenarios.
operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated user's profile, containing their basic identity and account settings. This operation ensures only the user themself can access their own data; no IDs are exposed or required in the path because 'me' references the current session or JWT. 

Authentication is mandatory; unauthenticated requests are rejected. The response mirrors the database structure: email (unique, immutable), display name (user-controlled), is_verified (reflecting email verification state), is_active (account enabled/disabled), and audit timestamps. All sensitive data such as password hash are excluded. The endpoint ensures no other user's data can be accessed via 'me'.

Other user-related endpoints (admin search, system logs of user activity) are separate and not included in 'me'. All business logic for 'me' is validated at the provider layer for secure and accurate information delivery.
operations.summary: Retrieve the authenticated user's profile information from the users table.

responseBody.description: Full profile data for the logged-in user only, reflecting todo_list_users fields marked for identity/business use.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation updates the authenticated user's own profile information in the users table (todo_list_users). The editable fields are only those allowed by business policy—for this application, it typically means display name and possibly feature/status flags. Email is immutable after signup, and changes to the password must go through dedicated security procedures. The operation requires authentication via a valid session/JWT: only the owner of the account can modify their own profile. All validation (required fields, allowed value ranges for display name, audit of modification etc.) is performed according to the schema and business requirements. The response returns the updated user record for confirmation.
operations.description:
Update the profile information for the currently authenticated user. This endpoint allows users to update mutable fields in their own profile, such as display name (global uniqueness not enforced per schema). Email address changes are not permitted by policy and require dedicated flows; password changes are handled elsewhere. 

Requests must be authenticated and reference the current session/JWT context, with all input validated for correctness and completeness. Only allowed fields are updatable; others will be ignored or cause validation failure. The operation returns the updated user object so clients can reflect UI changes or perform post-update logic. Audit timestamps are updated per business rules, and changes are logged for compliance purposes.

All update logic is driven from the todo_list_users table and respects any policy constraints on allowed self-updates. Security checks prevent one user from updating another's profile via this endpoint.
operations.summary: Update profile fields of the currently authenticated user in the users table.

requestBody.description: Fields to update for the current user, e.g. display name. Email and password updates are not permitted via this endpoint.

responseBody.description: Updated profile record for the authenticated user.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes the authenticated user's own account, irreversibly removing their user record from the todo_list_users table along with all owned todos from todo_list_todos and all related authentication/session records. The operation is available only to authenticated users and ensures that only a user can delete themself—no other actor can execute this operation. On success, all user and related data are purged from persistent storage, and authentication is immediately revoked. This action is final and non-recoverable, aligning with the business requirement for strict individual data privacy and irreversible removal.
operations.summary: Permanently delete the authenticated user's own account (todo_list_users).
operations.description:
Delete the current authenticated user's account and all owned data, including todos and every authentication/session trace.

This operation is restricted to the user themselves—no account can be deleted by anyone else, and no restoration, recovery, or cross-user deletion is permitted. Access is strictly controlled at the business logic and API middleware layer. On successful execution, the user's account row from todo_list_users, all records from todo_list_todos belonging to the user, and all session/audit records are fully and permanently removed from the database.

Security and privacy are paramount: this operation is only accessible to authenticated users, and triggers immediate token/session revocation along with all downstream deletions. All Prisma schema business rules regarding foreign keys and parent-child relationships are enforced for database consistency. Attempting to delete an account that does not belong to the requester or that is not authenticated results in a clear access denied error. There is no soft-deletion or retention—the removal is complete and all data is purged.

The operation assumes the user is certain about deletion, as recovery is impossible. All session tokens are invalidated, and any further access will require registration of a new account.
operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated list of active and historical authentication sessions for the authenticated user, as tracked in the todo_list_user_sessions table. Each session record includes relevant metadata (ip, href, referrer, creation/expiration times) associated with the user's sign-ins and token lifecycles. This allows users to audit their own login activity and session history for privacy and self-monitoring. The listing is available only to the authenticated user and never exposes data from other accounts. Security and pagination requirements ensure safe, performant access with user context isolation enforced in both business logic and database queries.
operations.summary: Retrieve a paginated list of the authenticated user's own session records (todo_list_user_sessions).
operations.description:
Fetch a paginated/searchable list of all login and authentication sessions for the currently logged-in user, as stored in the todo_list_user_sessions table.

This operation helps users monitor their own authentication history and manage their security posture. It exposes session metadata such as originating IP address, the URL/login context, referrer, session creation time, and expiration. All records pertain only to the requesting user—cross-user access is never allowed, and attempts are denied by both API logic and database filtering, following strict Prisma schema business rules.

The API supports complex search and pagination via filter criteria on fields such as session start/end dates and status. Sessions are ordered by creation date (most recent first) for usability. Security is enforced at both the endpoint and service layer: only the authenticated user can access this information about themselves, and attempts by unauthenticated or other actors are rejected. The maximum page size per response follows performance and privacy guidelines (see requirements), and error scenarios (such as invalid paging parameters or unauthorized access) trigger clear, standard error messages.

No session deletion or cross-user audit is ever allowed via this endpoint; this is strictly for self-service access by the account owner only.

requestBody.description: Filter, sorting, and pagination parameters to select relevant user session records.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of the current user's authentication session records for audit and self-service review.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves details of a specific session for the currently authenticated user in the todo-list application. It operates on the 'todo_list_user_sessions' Prisma table, which tracks every individual authentication session for audit and lifecycle management. The operation validates session ownership (only your own sessions can be fetched), and returns all session metadata fields including creation, expiration, and connection context. It references the user based on current authentication context rather than an explicit parameter. The sessionId is a UUID path parameter referring to the precise session instance. The response structure matches the ITodoListUserSession DTO. Uses the session's primary key, and enforces that users can only view their own session logs, not others. No cross-account session viewing allowed.
operations.description:
Retrieve details about a specific login session for the currently authenticated user.

This API allows a user to see details such as the originating IP, creation and expiration timestamps, and context information for a single session. Only the owner of the session may use this endpoint; administrators and other users may not retrieve session data for another user for privacy and security.

The sessionId parameter is the unique identifier of the desired authentication session, as stored in the 'todo_list_user_sessions' table. The system enforces that the session belongs to the currently logged-in account. This ensures secure, audit-friendly API behavior and restricts information exposure to the account owner.

This operation supports account auditability and user transparency, but not administration of global session data. Session records remain after expiration for audit purposes, so users can view both active and expired sessions.

Related operations include session termination (DELETE /users/me/sessions/{sessionId}) and session listing (not shown here). Errors are returned for invalid sessionId or attempts to access another user's session.
operations.summary: Retrieve details about a login session (todo_list_user_sessions).

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target session belonging to the currently authenticated user. Must be a valid session UUID from the todo_list_user_sessions table.

responseBody.description: Session detail information for the specified sessionId.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation deletes (revokes) a specific user session in the todo-list application for the currently logged-in user. It operates on the 'todo_list_user_sessions' Prisma table, which manages authentication session logs and token context. The API endpoint terminates the session indicated by the sessionId parameter, ensuring only the session owner can perform this action. No cross-user deletions are permitted. This yields account-level security, where users may revoke their own device/device or browser sessions to force logout. Session expiration information is updated accordingly, and the session record remains in the log for audit tracking—no soft or hard deletion is performed. Attempting to delete a session not owned by the current user is forbidden and results in an error response. Response returns updated session status per ITodoListUserSession.
operations.description:
Delete a specific authentication session for the current user, revoking access for the identified browser or device.

This API endpoint enables a user to forcibly log out a particular session (such as an open tab or another device) from their 'todo_list_user_sessions' records. Deletion here means marking the session as expired—actual session records remain for compliance and traceability, and no soft or hard deletion occurs. Only the session owner may perform this operation; system or admin-initiated deletions are handled elsewhere. Attempts to delete another user's session will be denied.

Security is strictly enforced by verifying both authentication and sessionId ownership before performing the operation. This enables users to maintain account security by revoking lost or suspicious sessions on demand.

Related endpoints include viewing session details (GET /users/me/sessions/{sessionId}) and listing all current sessions.
operations.summary: Revoke and expire an authentication session (todo_list_user_sessions).

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the session to be revoked, belonging to the currently authenticated user.

responseBody.description: Session status after revocation, reflecting updated expiration state.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: Retrieves a paginated and filtered list of all email verification events for the currently authenticated user. This operation is based on the todo_list_user_email_verifications Prisma table, which tracks all email verification tokens sent to a user, their issue/consumption/expiration states, and security audit lifecycle. It supports audit, compliance, and user self-service scenarios by returning the full history of verification email and token issuances, redemptions, and expirations tied to the currently logged-in user. The operation enables filtering by creation date or status as defined by business requirements. It only returns events belonging to the authenticated user (identity derived from authentication context), ensuring privacy and strictly scoped data access. Underlying data includes creation timestamps, consume state, associated token string (partially masked), and expiration state.
operations.description:
Retrieves a filtered, paginated history of all email verification events for the currently authenticated user.

This operation provides the user the ability to review every email verification token that has been issued for their account, including both successful redemptions and expired/unredeemed tokens. It allows for audit trails, troubleshooting of account validation, and visibility into security-related activity such as repeat verification attempts or expired links.

The API sources data from the todo_list_user_email_verifications Prisma model, limiting all returned events to only those owned by the current authenticated user. Sensitive properties such as verification_token should be partially masked and never shown fully in responses (implementation detail). The operation supports optional filtering by creation date or verification status, and results are paginated for usability. Only the authenticated user can access their own verification logs. Related operations include fetching specific verification event details and executing redemption via the 'at' operation below.
operations.summary: List email verification events for current user (todo_list_user_email_verifications)

requestBody.description: Optional search and pagination parameters to filter the user's email verification history (e.g., by status or date).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of email verification history for the current user, with optional filters applied. Each record summarizes a single verification event.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Retrieves details for a specific email verification event for the authenticated user, as identified by the unique verification_token path parameter. This operation maps to the todo_list_user_email_verifications table, providing metadata about a single verification email/token usage: including issue time, expiration, consumption status and related security audit properties. The endpoint can be used to allow client-side redemption, checking of token state, or for troubleshooting by the user. Strict validation ensures that only the owner (authenticated user) can access their corresponding token event, and tokens issued to different users are never accessible. The path parameter matches the unique verification_token field (which is unique per event in the schema), allowing for direct retrieval and validation at the API level. This operation forms the read basis for subsequent token redemption or status checks.
operations.description:
Fetches full detail about a specific email verification event for the currently authenticated user, identified via the verification token present in the path parameter.

This operation allows a user to view metadata regarding any particular verification email/token issued to them, including the issue timestamp, whether the token was redeemed/expired, and other key event properties, as defined in the todo_list_user_email_verifications Prisma model. Only events belonging to the current authenticated user relative to the session may be accessed; querying another user's token (even if the token is known) is strictly disallowed for confidentiality and security.

The API guarantees both existence and ownership of the event before responding, and errors appropriately if the token does not belong to the authenticated user. The returned structure contains all event fields except sensitive values like the full verification token (which may be partially masked or omitted for security). This is used for redemption, auditing, or support flows.
operations.summary: Get details for a user's specific email verification event by token (todo_list_user_email_verifications)

parameters.name: verificationToken
parameters.description: Verification token string uniquely identifying a single email verification event for this user. Case-sensitive and unique per event (see schema).

responseBody.description: Full detail about the requested email verification event belonging to the current user, excluding sensitive values.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated and filterable history of password reset requests/events for the authenticated user in the Todo List system. It operates on the todo_list_user_password_resets table, providing security and audit transparency by allowing users to see if and when password reset links were generated, expired, or redeemed for their account. This supports user-driven security review, suspicious activity detection, and transparency over past and active reset flows. Filtering, pagination, and sorting are supported to navigate large histories.
operations.summary: Retrieve password reset history for the authenticated user's account using the password reset log table.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows an authenticated user to query the log of all password reset requests and their status for their own account. Results include events whether used, expired, or still active. The operation supports filtering by date range, token status (expired/used/active), and is ordered by creation time for ease of review.

Security is critical: only the owner of the account may access their own password reset event history. The operation relies on user identity provided by authentication context, not a path parameter, so no sensitive user ID is directly exchanged or exposed. Rate limiting is enforced to prevent probing, and data is filtered strictly for the authenticated user only.

This history is sourced from the todo_list_user_password_resets table. Each item includes timestamps for issuance, expiry, and redemption/consumption. This operation can be used in account security dashboards, help users recognize unwanted resets, and provide a compliance trail for security events. Related operations: GET /users/me/passwordResets/{resetToken} for inspecting a single reset event in detail.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and pagination parameters for password reset event history on the user's account.

responseBody.description: Paginated and filterable list of the user's password reset history, including each event's status and metadata.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information for a specific password reset event for the authenticated user. It operates on a single event from the todo_list_user_password_resets table, identified by its unique reset token. It confirms ownership, presents all relevant timestamps, and allows the user to check whether the link is still active, when it was created, when it will expire, and if it has already been consumed. This is essential for self-service auditing, helping users to validate and investigate password reset events.
operations.summary: Retrieve details for a password reset event by token for the user's account using the password reset log table.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows the authenticated user to inspect the details of a password reset event from their own account by specifying the event's unique reset token in the path. Information returned includes creation, expiration, and consumption timestamps, as well as verification that the reset token belongs to the querying user and has not been used or expired.

Strict security and privacy controls are enforced: only the user who owns the reset token may access its event details, and tokens are checked for validity, expiration, and ownership. The token parameter does not expose the internal reset event ID, but is a single-use, cryptographically strong identifier.

The operation references the todo_list_user_password_resets table, returning all related event information for UI display or suspicious activity review. If the token is invalid or no longer associated with the authenticated user, a not-found or error response is returned. Related operation: PATCH /users/me/passwordResets for listing all events.

parameters.name: resetToken
parameters.description: Unique, single-use password reset token for identifying the reset event (scoped to the authenticated user).

responseBody.description: Password reset event information, including metadata and security-related timestamps.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation provides advanced searching and retrieval of todo list items across all users, supporting filtering, pagination, and sorting. It operates on the todo_list_todos table in the Prisma schema, leveraging all defined fields for precise querying. The search capabilities are designed for flexibility, enabling queries by text, completion state, due date ranges, and linked user. Results are paginated and may be sorted by various attributes as defined in business requirements.
operations.description:
Search and filter todo list items matching user-supplied criteria with support for pagination and flexible sorting.

This endpoint enables users and admins to retrieve lists of todo items, specifying criteria such as completion status, associated user, and time range.

Security and filtering considerations are implemented according to the requesting user's role and permissions. Only items visible or accessible to the user will be returned. Pagination prevents overloading responses, while input validation and error handling protect against malformed queries or constraint violations.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of todo items from todo_list_todos table

requestBody.description: Search and filtering parameters for todo items (completion state, user, query, pagination, etc.)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo item summaries matching the search criteria, as defined in ITodoListTodo.ISummary.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the detailed information for a specific todo item, identified by its unique ID. It interacts directly with the todo_list_todos table in the Prisma schema. The endpoint ensures that users can view only items they are authorized to access, enforcing appropriate filtering by user or permissions as applicable.
operations.description:
Obtain full detail for a specific todo item by its unique identifier.

This endpoint is designed to provide complete information for a particular todo item, including all fields and metadata stored in the database. Permissions and access control ensure that only authorized users can retrieve this information.

The response structure complies with the ITodoListTodo data model, providing clients with all attributes necessary for viewing, editing, or auditing the todo item. Error responses handle cases where the todo item does not exist or access is denied.
operations.summary: Retrieve complete details about a specific todo item by ID from todo_list_todos table

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item (UUID format, as defined by todo_list_todos schema)

responseBody.description: Full todo item details as defined in ITodoListTodo.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo item in the todo_list_todos table. It allows an authenticated user to generate a unique, actionable task with required title and optional detail fields. Each todo is strictly owned by the creating user, linked through a mandatory foreign key to todo_list_users. All business validation rules for fields such as title trim length, permissible due date (present/future), and correct data types are enforced at the application layer before persisting the entity. Temporal system fields including creation, update, and (if relevant) completion timestamps are set automatically. The response returns the newly created todo with all metadata, ensuring immediate feedback and seamless UI updates for the user.
operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the current authenticated user. The operation requires at minimum a trimmed, non-empty title between 1 and 100 characters, which must be unique within the user's list for business logic clarity, though not enforced at the database level.

Optionally, the user may specify a description (up to 1000 characters) and a due date restricted to the present or future (ISO 8601 UTC format). Initial completion status is always false unless explicitly provided; completed_at must be null at creation. All timestamps (created_at/updated_at) are generated by the system upon insertion.

Authentication is mandatory, and the creating user is assigned as the owner via the session/user principal without needing to pass a user ID in the request. Immediate error responses are produced for invalid title length, improperly formatted due dates, or attempts to create todos for other users. This endpoint is the standard entry for all todo creation workflows in the system.
operations.summary: Create a new todo item in todo_list_todos.

requestBody.description: Information necessary to create a new todo item for the authenticated user.

responseBody.description: The newly created todo item with all metadata and owner linkage.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing todo item owned by the current authenticated user in the todo_list_todos table. The endpoint facilitates editing of core business fields such as title, description, due_date, and toggling of is_completed. Field-level business logic is enforced, including validation of title length, description length, date format, and is_completed state transitions. Timestamps for updated_at (system-managed) and completed_at (system-managed for is_completed transition) are applied automatically, supporting UI synchronization and auditability. The update is restricted to the owner, with user context determined implicitly from authentication without explicit user ID fields in the request or path. The response returns the updated todo item reflecting all new values.
operations.description:
Update an existing todo item belonging to the authenticated user. The todoId parameter uniquely identifies the target todo, which must be owned by the requesting user, preventing unauthorized access or edits.

Field updates may include a new title (validated for trim and length), a description (up to 1000 characters), a due date (present or future, ISO 8601 format), and changes to completion status (is_completed and completed_at handled automatically). System-managed columns updated_at and, if applicable, completed_at are set at the time of update by the service logic. Any transition of is_completed from false to true also updates completed_at; resetting to false clears it.

Attempting to update a todo not owned by the user, or passing invalid field data (e.g., too long title/description, invalid dates, unauthorized changes to other users' todos) results in a clear error. All validation rules reflect the strict requirements and privacy model of the todo_list_todos schema.
operations.summary: Update an existing todo item in todo_list_todos by unique todoId.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item to update.

requestBody.description: Fields and values to update for the specified todo item.

responseBody.description: The updated todo item with all current business and audit fields.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: A todo item must be created before it can be updated. The 'todoId' required for update is generated by the creation operation.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently removes a single todo item from the system. It maps directly to the todo_list_todos table in the database. The operation deletes the todo specified by its unique identifier, provided as the path parameter. Deletion is allowed only by the owning user, and strict access control is enforced; only the user that owns the todo can erase it. All fields, including audit timestamps, are removed from persistence with this action. There is no soft-delete or archival mechanism—removal is a true data deletion per the schema, conforming to the single-user privacy focus of the todo list app.

Error conditions include attempting to delete a todo that does not exist or does not belong to the requesting user, in which cases appropriate error responses (404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden) are issued. This endpoint should be called only when the user intentionally wants to irreversibly erase a todo from their private set. Other CRUD actions (create, update, read) should be performed via the corresponding endpoints.
operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo item that belongs to the authenticated user. This endpoint directly erases the specified todo from the todo_list_todos table.

Only the owner of the todo is permitted to perform this operation. Authentication and authorization must be enforced at the application layer to guarantee that each user can manage only their own todos. Attempting to access or delete another user's todo will result in a forbidden error.

Upon successful deletion, all information for the deleted todo is immediately and irreversibly removed from persistent storage. This action does not support recovery, soft delete, or undo. Auditability is provided by the system's timestamping prior to deletion, but the record itself will not exist after this operation. If the todo does not exist or the id is invalid, a 404 Not Found error is returned.

This operation should be used when the user intends to irreversibly remove a task from their todo list, such as to clean up completed or abandoned tasks. It is recommended to confirm user intent in the UI before invoking this endpoint, as recovery is impossible post-deletion.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a todo item from the todo_list_todos table.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo to delete (UUID format).

operations.name: erase

authorizations.name: user
authorizations.description: A registered user who can create, view, update, complete, and delete their own todo items. Can register, authenticate, and manage only their own account and todos.

limit.description: Limitation of records per a page.

Total pages.

Equal to {@link records} / {@link limit} with ceiling.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

ITodoListUser.IJoin.description:
Registration payload for a new Todo List user.

Required properties are strictly aligned to the todo_list_users table and incorporate the atomic onboarding workflow. Accepts a unique email address and plain-text password for account creation, not the hashed value. The email is globally unique, cannot be changed after registration, and must follow RFC 5322 format. On submit, the account is created in an unverified state and will require email verification before activation.

Session context fields are included for audit trail and security (connection URL, referrer URL, client IP). These properties support detailed logging and fraud detection. Password is never returned in responses and only sent here for hashing and credential creation.

email.description: User's unique email address (RFC 5322). Used as the global identifier for new Todo List user accounts. Must be unique, lowercase, and cannot be changed after signup.

password.description: Plain-text password for registration. Will be securely hashed server-side and never stored or returned in plain form.

display_name.description: Display name for the user. Shown in the user's profile and may be modified after account creation.

oneOf.description: Client's IP address for the session. May be IPv4 or IPv6.
Client's IPv6 address. Used when available.
Field may be left null, in which case the server will infer IP from the request origin.

ip.description: Client's originating IP address for registration session audit. Used for security analytics and fraud detection. Optional (server will extract if not provided).

href.description: The full connection URL at the time of registration (client-side page URL). Required for session logging and security analytics.

referrer.description: The referrer URL at registration (origin page). Used for session analysis and may be an empty string for direct access.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication and token response after registration, login, or token refresh for Todo List users.

Represents the secure payload issued when a user joins, authenticates, or refreshes their session. Contains user identity (id), a JWT-based authentication token object, and the user's registration and status profile as appropriate. All password fields are excluded from this DTO for security.

The token field references IAuthorizationToken, which holds the JWT token pair. The user field references ITodoListUser.ISummary, which provides the essential public-facing user properties. Any confidential data (e.g., password hash) is omitted.

This DTO is consumed by clients for authenticated session establishment and renewal only.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated user account (UUID, from the todo_list_users primary key).

email.description:
The registered email address for the account, used as the unique global login credential and for all system notifications.

The email address must be valid per RFC 5322 and is strictly unique and immutable once set. This field is never exposed in search APIs and always hidden except in "my profile" views.

display_name.description:
The user's display name, visible in personal dashboards and application UI.

While not required to be globally unique, it must be present and remain within 100 characters per business rules. Users can update their display name any time, subject to validation constraints.

is_verified.description:
Indicates whether the user's email address has been verified through system confirmation flows.

Set to true only after the email verification link has been consumed. Controls UI display and feature unlock.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether the account is currently enabled for login and interaction.

Set to false in cases of permanent deletion, security suspension, or user-initiated deactivation. New logins are rejected when false.

created_at.description:
Date and time of initial registration and account creation, stored in UTC ISO 8601 format.

This field is set once by the system and cannot be modified by users. Used for audit and eligibility checks.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent change to the account record (profile updates, credential changes, etc.), in UTC ISO 8601 format.

System-managed for audit and support purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the account was permanently deleted (if applicable), in UTC ISO 8601 format. Null if account is still active.

Set only during irreversible deletion flows. Otherwise remains empty.

user.description: Summary profile of the authenticated user, containing public-facing and business-critical properties only.

ITodoListUser.ISummary.description:
Summary public profile for a Todo List user account.

Contains the primary identifying, public profile, and status fields necessary to display essential account information, enable access control, and support system audit trails.

Sensitive fields like password hashes and any internal security data are excluded. This form supports lightweight lists, session tokens, and general UI display requirements.

All fields must correspond directly to the columns in the todo_list_users database table. For privacy, deleted accounts show deletion timestamp for audit but are not accessible for authentication or public presentation.

id.description:
User account unique identifier (UUID, from todo_list_users primary key).

Serves as the global reference for the user's account across all authentication, authorization, and business logic operations.

email.description:
Registered email address, globally unique, used as the immutable username for authentication and all system notifications.

Email is strictly validated (RFC 5322), does not change, and is never duplicated across accounts.

display_name.description: User's chosen display name, visible in UI profile contexts. Modifiable by the user (within business constraints), intended solely for aesthetic or community purposes. Not required to be globally unique but must always be present.

is_verified.description:
Indicates whether the user's email address has been successfully verified and activated by consumption of the system's verification process.

A verified status is required before user login or access.

is_active.description:
Current enabled/disabled (active/inactive) status of the account.

Set to false for suspended, permanently deleted, or otherwise unusable accounts. Controls authorization eligibility and login acceptance.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of when the account was first created (UTC ISO 8601).

Immutable after registration. Used for audit, eligibility, and system reporting.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last update action on this account (profile, credential, or status change). Stored in UTC ISO 8601.

Business flows may update this timestamp at any profile or credential change.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp of permanent account deletion if applicable (UTC ISO 8601). Null if the account is still active.

Used only for audit and legal compliance. Deleted users cannot be accessed or authenticated and do not appear in normal searches.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
Login credential schema for Todo List user authentication.

Represents the user's credential input required for logging in. Requires both the user's unique email address and password (checked against the stored hash in the database). Email must match a verified and active account.

Context fields (href, referrer, ip) provide environmental and session risk context for authentication audit. No authentication tokens or profile data are returned by this schema; this is strictly for credential intake.

email.description:
The user's unique email address, used as account identifier for login.

Must match an existing todo_list_users account and comply with RFC 5322 formatting. Case-insensitive and required for credential verification.

password.description:
User's plain text password for login only (never stored). Checked against the securely stored password_hash in the database.

Immediately discarded after successful or failed authentication.

href.description:
URL where the login form was submitted (current browser/application location).

Used for audit, security analytics, and tracking session context. Required for audit trail consistency.

referrer.description:
Referring URL leading to the login attempt. May be empty if direct navigation.

Important for session and analytics context in risk mitigation and fraud analysis workflows.

oneOf.description: IPv4 address of the client, if available.
IPv6 address, supported for clients using the newer protocol.
Null if IP not provided by client. Backend will auto-detect if possible.

ip.description:
Client's IP address used for credential submission, risk scoring, session record context, and authentication logging.

Supplied for full security audit and advanced policy enforcement. Optional and may be null.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token submission schema for obtaining new JWT tokens for an authenticated Todo List user session.

This schema represents the required input for the token refresh operation. The client provides a valid, currently active refresh token previously issued by the system. The backend validates this token based on session and user security constraints before issuing new tokens. If the refresh token is invalid/expired, authentication is denied, requiring new login.

No additional business fields are required in this schema. The token value binds the session, user identity, and security context to the authentication framework.

refresh_token.description: The valid and active refresh token issued during a prior authentication operation. Must be unexpired and recognized, as tracked in the authentication session database. Required for requesting token renewal.

verification_token.description:
Verification token received via email.

This token must be provided by the user to complete the email verification process. The token is a unique, randomly-generated, single-use string bound to the user account and stored in the database. It is required for redeeming the verification event and cannot be empty.

ITodoListUserEmailVerification.IVerify.description:
Payload for verifying a user's email using a verification token.

This schema represents the expected request body during the email verification process in user onboarding. Clients must provide the token sent via email, which is checked for validity, expiry, and prior use. Upon acceptance, the user's account becomes active.

The payload must include the verification_token as issued in the verification email.

success.description:
Indicates if the verification was successful and user's account has become active.

True if the provided verification token was valid, not expired, and not previously consumed.

message.description:
Feedback message describing the result of the verification process.

This message provides user-facing context such as success confirmation or the specific nature of any failure (e.g., expired, already used, or invalid token). It facilitates user guidance and improves UX for failed attempts.

ITodoListUserEmailVerification.IVerified.description:
Minimal response returned after attempting email verification.

Indicates whether the account was activated as a result of verifying the token. Includes a human-readable message, suitable for user interfaces, that describes the outcome (success or any error condition).

This response schema is used for both success and failure scenarios, supporting robust error handling and clear communication with the user.

ITodoListUserPasswordReset.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for initiating the password reset process for a user in the Todo List system.

Accepts the email address of the account to initiate a password reset event. Email must be valid and normalized. No user-identifying or sensitive data is leaked regardless of outcome, for privacy and security. Always responds generically to prevent user enumeration.

This payload is used in the endpoint to request a password reset. When the target user exists, a one-time, time-limited reset token is generated and sent to their email. If not, the response is indistinguishable, preserving privacy.

Validation is strictly enforced on the email format. Reset event is registered in the password resets audit log for security, rate limiting, and future reference.

No actual password is accepted in this step; the actual reset occurs via a separate endpoint redeeming the issued token.

email.description:
The email address of the account for which to initiate password reset.

Must be a valid, normalized email. Used to locate the user account if present, but response does not reveal account existence. This property is required.

ITodoListUserPasswordReset.IRequested.description:
Minimal response DTO after a password reset request has been initiated for a user.

This DTO never reveals whether the requested account exists or not, for privacy and anti-enumeration security. Used to indicate that the reset process has begun (if account exists) or to return a generic completion (if not). Intended strictly for confirming to the client that the request was accepted and is being handled.

No user data or reset token is ever included. For user security and privacy.

message.description:
Confirmation or generic message indicating the password reset process has been initiated, regardless of user account presence.

Never leaks information about user existence, always formulated generically (for example, 'If an account with this email exists, a reset link has been sent.').

ITodoListUserPasswordReset.IReset.description:
Request payload for redeeming a password reset token. Used to submit a new password and the one-time reset token issued via 'todo_list_user_password_resets'. If the reset token is valid, unexpired, and unused, this creates an atomic password update in 'todo_list_users' and marks the token as consumed.

This operation is security-sensitive and audited fully for traceability and compliance. All inputs are validated—token must match a current unused row in 'todo_list_user_password_resets' and password must satisfy server-side validation rules.

The token is single-use and has strict expiry. On success, the user's password hash is updated; failure returns a generic error to prevent probing.

Used by clients who possess a valid password reset link/token (delivered via email or other secure channel).

reset_token.description: The one-time password reset token previously issued and delivered to the user. Must exactly match an unexpired, unused token in 'todo_list_user_password_resets'. Used as the secure credential to authorize a password change event.

password.description: Plain new password selected by the user for account authentication. Must meet all system password policy requirements (length, complexity, etc). Will be securely hashed by the backend and stored in 'todo_list_users.password_hash'. Never sent or stored in plaintext at rest.

ITodoListUserPasswordReset.IResetResult.description:
Minimal result returned by password reset redemption.

Indicates whether the supplied token/password combination resulted in a successful password change. Does not leak info about validity of the token for security reasons. Used to confirm flow completion after a POST to /auth/user/reset-password.

reset.description: Whether the password reset (token redemption and password change) was successful. 'true' on success, 'false' if token was invalid, expired, or consumed. No additional information is returned for security reasons.

ITodoListUser.IChangePassword.description:
Payload for changing the password of an authenticated user within the Todo List service.

The object requires both the user's current (old) password and the new desired password, to ensure security and prevent unauthorized changes. The old password is compared against the original database hash (see 'password_hash' in the 'todo_list_users' Prisma model), and, upon verification, the backend system updates the stored hash to correspond to the new password after proper cryptographic processing.

The process is permitted only for accounts that are both active and verified (see 'is_active' and 'is_verified' in the underlying model), and all necessary validation and account update logic is coordinated by the API.

This schema must not include the user id or authentication context fields—actor ownership is deduced from the JWT or current session. The backend enforces all security and lifecycle rules associated with account credential updates.

Used strictly for atomic, authenticated password change operations for existing users—never for user registration, admin resets, or password recovery flows.

old_password.description: The user's current password (plain text), provided to verify that the submitter legitimately owns the account. This value is not stored or logged, only compared with the hashed value from the database for authentication. Must be at least 8 characters.

new_password.description: The new password (plain text) the user wishes to set. This will be cryptographically validated and, if accepted by password policy, stored as a secure hash in the 'password_hash' field (the hash is never directly exposed). Must be at least 8 characters and satisfy password complexity rules enforced by the backend. This value is never stored as plain text.

ITodoListUser.IChangePasswordResult.description:
Minimal response indicating the result of the password change operation for an authenticated Todo List user.

Success is indicated by the presence of 'success': true. If the change is denied (for example, if the old password is incorrect or password policy fails), 'success' is false and the 'reason' property is provided with a short, user-facing error description.

This schema is designed for atomic, authenticated credential updates only and should not be used for user registration, admin operations, or recovery.

success.description: Indicates if the password change was successful. If true, the password was updated and the session remains usable; if false, the operation failed (see 'reason').

reason.description: Short message describing the reason the password change failed. Only present if 'success' is false. Examples: 'Incorrect current password', 'Password does not meet complexity requirements', 'Account disabled'.

ITodoListUser.ILogoutResult.description:
Result object returned after successful user logout.

Indicates that all active sessions and tokens for the current authenticated user have been invalidated and marked as expired in the audit trail. This type is used as the response body for the logout endpoint and confirms enforcement of security measures.

Contains only minimal properties, since logout conveys a status rather than returning data. Used to communicate a successful operation for UI feedback and auditing.

success.description: Indicates whether the logout operation was completed successfully. True means all sessions were invalidated and tokens revoked.

ITodoListUser.IDeletionResult.description:
Result object returned after permanent user account deletion.

Indicates whether the account and all associated data were irreversibly removed and the operation completed as requested. Used as the response body for the account erasure endpoint.

Minimal by design—intended for UI feedback, not to return sensitive or structural data. Operation is always authenticated, and returns false only when deletion fails for internal reasons or is blocked by policy.

success.description: Indicates whether the account erasure operation was successful. True means the user and all related data have been deleted irreversibly.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the user account. This value is generated by the system upon registration and cannot be changed.

Used as the primary key for user records and referenced by all authentication and business logic. Always returned for profile queries but never exposed in unauthenticated APIs.

email.description:
The registered email address for the account, used as the unique global login credential and for all system notifications.

The email address must be valid per RFC 5322 and is strictly unique and immutable once set. This field is never exposed in search APIs and always hidden except in "my profile" views.

display_name.description:
The user's display name, visible in personal dashboards and application UI.

While not required to be globally unique, it must be present and remain within 100 characters per business rules. Users can update their display name any time, subject to validation constraints.

is_verified.description:
Indicates whether the user's email address has been verified through system confirmation flows.

Set to true only after the email verification link has been consumed. Controls UI display and feature unlock.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether the account is currently enabled for login and interaction.

Set to false in cases of permanent deletion, security suspension, or user-initiated deactivation. New logins are rejected when false.

created_at.description:
Date and time of initial registration and account creation, stored in UTC ISO 8601 format.

This field is set once by the system and cannot be modified by users. Used for audit and eligibility checks.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent change to the account record (profile updates, credential changes, etc.), in UTC ISO 8601 format.

System-managed for audit and support purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the account was permanently deleted (if applicable), in UTC ISO 8601 format. Null if account is still active.

Set only during irreversible deletion flows. Otherwise remains empty.

ITodoListUser.description:
Registered Todo List application user profile.

Represents the identity, authentication, and business presence of each unique user account. Core fields include immutable login credential (email), updatable display name, and status/audit flags. All sensitive/internal authentication values (such as password hash) are strictly omitted in all API responses.

Ownership of all todo items is tied to this identity, and users manage only their own information. This schema is used in profile views, account settings pages, and authorization verification endpoints.

Readonly fields (id, email, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are guaranteed safe for display. Mutability is targeted for display_name, with verification and activation states controlled by the system.

display_name.description: New display name to update for the authenticated user profile. Must be present and within 100 characters per business validation. Name is not globally unique, and can be changed by user at any time.

is_active.description: (Admin or system use only) Desired active status for the user account. Self-service update endpoints ignore this field, but it may appear in admin or system-automation APIs.

is_verified.description: (System controlled) Email verification status. Direct user update is NOT allowed. Managed via verification flows only.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
Fields allowed for update by the authenticated user on their own profile.

Only display_name is intended to be editable directly by users via self-service update APIs. Other fields (is_active, is_verified) may only be set by admin or automation; user updates to those are ignored or rejected.

Update logic applies validation for length, presence, and format as enforced by business requirements and the underlying database. Email and password are never modifiable through this interface; use dedicated flows instead.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
Authentication session audit entity for user logins in the Todo List app.

Represents an individual login or token session for a user, storing session context data for audit trails, security monitoring, and self-service session management. Each record is linked to a specific user and includes metadata such as originating IP address, login context (href), HTTP referrer, creation and expiration timestamps. Used for tracking multiple concurrent logins, session expiry, and session revocation. Immutable ownership—sessions are strictly user-bound and never transferred between users.

API responses expose the full session record for authenticated users for privacy monitoring, with strict access to only a user's own sessions enforced in all endpoints.

id.description: Primary key—unique identifier of this session record. Generated as a UUID for each session event.

todo_list_user_id.description: Foreign key referencing the owning user account (todo_list_users.id). Determines strict session-user binding for access control and relation context.

ip.description: IP address (IPv4/IPv6 as string) from which session was created. Used for risk analysis, anomaly detection, and audit tracing.

href.description: Original URL where session was created (login or sign-in page). Supports security, analytics, and user support for investigating session context.

referrer.description: HTTP referrer at session initiation. Documents session origin for traceability, privacy compliance, and security investigation.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this session was created (UTC, ISO 8601). Represents login or session establishment time for lifecycle auditing, ordering, and analytics.

oneOf.description: Session expiration time (UTC, ISO 8601). Indicates when the session or token became invalid. Null if the session is still valid.
Null if session is currently valid.

expired_at.description: The timestamp for when the session was invalidated or expired, or null if still active.

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:
Request object for filtering, searching, and paginating user session audit records.

Used in endpoints for retrieving a user's authentication session history. Supports criteria for search by session start/end date, ordering, and pagination. Parameters are subject to system- or policy-enforced bounds (e.g., date ranges, max page size). This DTO is only accepted for the authenticated user's own sessions (never for others) and must not contain any identifying information about other users.

Enables feature-rich user-facing session lists compliant with security and privacy standards.

page.description: Page number for paginated session records (1-based index). Defaults to 1 if unspecified.

limit.description: Maximum number of session records per page for paging results. Enforced as a policy maximum for privacy and performance.

oneOf.description: Sort field for session records, allowed values are 'created_at' or 'expired_at' (sort by creation or expiration time).
Sort field for session records, allowed values are 'created_at' or 'expired_at' (sort by creation or expiration time).

Sort direction—ascending or descending.

from.description: Lower bound for session creation time in filter (UTC/ISO8601), or null if unbounded.

oneOf.description: Latest session creation timestamp (or ISO date) to include in results.

Primary identifier for this email verification event.

Represents a unique identifier generated for each event instance. Used for internal tracking, not exposed for token-based user retrieval.

todo_list_user_id.description:
Identifier of the user account this verification event belongs to.

Foreign key referencing todo_list_users.id. Always scoped to ownership by the authenticated user in this API. Never appears in external requests where actor is user.

verification_token.description:
Secure token string issued for the verification event.

Token is unique per event, tied to a single user, and is issued for email verification link delivery. Only the owner may access masked or partial values for audit. NEVER shown fully in standard API responses, only possibly in IInvert or for admin trace purposes.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the verification token was redeemed.

consumed_at.description:
Timestamp when this verification event was consumed via link activation.

Null when unused or expired.

expires_at.description:

created_at.description:
